SMTO-WEB-0056 — SMTO needs to know exactly which item you mean

GUID: 94cca746-bc5d-56f7-8be8-c3fb055805c2
Slug: research-entity-clarification-required
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • Your question names a specific item, but the web research only found similar ones, not that exact item. SMTO held back a final answer so it wouldn't give you facts about the wrong thing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If SMTO asks which item you meant, reply in the conversation with the exact name, full model number or version, or paste a link to the item's page. SMTO can only finish once it knows the exact item, and it uses your reply to look up that item.
  2. If SMTO offers a list of similar items, pick one only if it really is the item you want. Don't accept a close match just to get an answer. Facts about a similar item, like a different model year, can be wrong for the one you asked about.
  3. If you don't know the exact name, say so and ask SMTO for a partial answer that clearly states what it could not confirm. A partial answer that names its gaps is allowed; a full answer about an unconfirmed item is not.

What success looks like

  • SMTO gives an answer about the exact item you named, or a partial answer that clearly says which item it could not confirm.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, along with the exact item name you gave, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to just guess which item you meant.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof validation rejected an answered/completed web research result because one or more exact entities in the request are still unresolved (no exact match observed, only similar alternatives).

What this means

  • Unresolved entity blockers remain when completion claims answered or completed status. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • Unresolved entity blockers remain when completion claims answered or completed status.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect unresolved entity IDs, literal user text and blocked fields.

How to fix it

  • In _validate_answer (skills/web_research/validation.py) clarification_blockers is non-empty while the completion status is answered or completed. The agent must call ask_user with the unresolved research_entity_id, or finish with a validated partial limitation; similar identifiers in observed_alternatives are not substitutions. The check only applies when the completion.research_proof guard (Research proof validation in Agent Checks) is enabled.
  • Use ask_user with the unresolved research_entity_id, or finish with a validated partial limitation. Similar identifiers are not substitutions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The user resolves the exact identity or a validated partial response preserves the ambiguity.

What not to do

  • Do not guess an exact entity identity from ambiguous candidates.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
